title: Debounce and retry helpers
blurb: Two small utilities that are easy to get subtly wrong: a debounce with leading/trailing edges and a retry with backoff.
brief: Your team wants two dependency-free helpers: debounce (for search boxes and resize handlers) and retry (for flaky network calls). Both take an injectable timers object, { setTimeout, clearTimeout }, so the hidden tests can control time. If timers is omitted, use the real global functions. Implement debounce in debounce.js and retry in retry.js.
requirements: debounce(fn, waitMs, { leading = false, trailing = true, timers } = {}) returns a debounced function. fn must be a function, otherwise throw TypeError. waitMs must be a finite number >= 0, otherwise throw RangeError. leading and trailing may not both be false (RangeError).
Trailing (the default): fn is called once, waitMs after the most recent call, with the arguments and this of that most recent call. Every call restarts the wait.
Leading: the first call of a burst calls fn immediately with that call's arguments. A burst ends once waitMs passes with no calls.
With leading and trailing both true, fn also gets a trailing call, but only if the debounced function was called again during the burst. A single call must call fn exactly once.
The debounced function returns the result of the most recent call to fn (undefined before the first).
debounced.cancel() drops any pending call and ends the burst, so the next call starts a new burst (and fires the leading edge again).

debounced.flush() runs a pending trailing call now, with its latest arguments, and returns fn's result. If nothing is pending it does nothing and returns the last result. After a flush the pending timer must not fire again.
debounced.pending() is true while a trailing call is scheduled.

retry(task, { attempts = 3, baseMs = 100, factor = 2, maxMs = Infinity, shouldRetry = () => true, timers } = {}, callback) runs task(cb) right away. task reports with cb(err, value). task and callback must be functions (TypeError). attempts must be a positive integer, baseMs a finite number >= 0, factor a number >= 1 and maxMs a number >= 0 (Infinity is allowed), otherwise RangeError.
If cb receives no error, call callback(null, value) once and stop. attempts is the total number of tries, so attempts: 1 never retries.

If cb receives an error and there are tries left and shouldRetry(err, n) is true, where n is the 1-based number of the try that just failed, run task again after min(maxMs, baseMs * factor ** (n - 1)) ms. Otherwise call callback(err) at once with that last error and do not wait.
task may call cb more than once. Only the first call for each try counts.
retry returns { cancel() }. cancel() clears any pending wait, and after it callback is never called, even if an in-flight task calls cb later. Cancelling after the callback has run does nothing.
